scenario.name: Tokenised asset launch
scenario.why: A tokenised product goes from idea to a tested contract.

trigger.msg: Can we launch tokenised invoice financing next quarter?

actions.summary: Write token rules and compliance requirements

sections.text: Define who may hold, transfer and redeem tokenised invoice units, and the compliance controls built into the contract.

items: Only KYC-verified wholesale investors may hold units
Transfers over $1,000 carry travel-rule data
Redemption at invoice maturity, T+2 settlement
Issuer can pause transfers under a 2-of-3 multisig
Monthly reserve attestation published on-chain
Secondary transfers between verified holders: allowed at launch?
Treatment of defaulted invoices in the redemption queue

actions.summary: Screen pilot investor wallets
Deploy the contract to a test network

items: 14:02 Compiled 4 contracts, 0 warnings
14:03 Deployed InvoiceToken v0.3
14:03 Allowlist seeded with 11 verified wallets
14:04 Pause and freeze functions verified
transfer() reverts unless both parties are on the allowlist
pause() restricted to the multisig
redeem() only after maturity timestamp

actions.summary: Run transfer and redemption tests

scenario.outcome: The tokenised invoice product is defined, screened and running on a test network. Mainnet deployment stays a human decision after the external audit.

scenario.name: Repayment reminders
scenario.why: Fewer missed BNPL repayments without breaking lending rules.

trigger.msg: Missed repayments are up 9%. Can we add smart reminders?

steps.handoff: Payday mismatch is the main driver

actions.summary: Analyse missed repayments by cohort
actions.result: Most misses are 1–3 days late, on payday mismatches

actions.summary: Create the reminders epic with stories

items: LEND-78 Remind me 2 days before a repayment is due
LEND-79 Let me move my repayment date to payday, once per term
LEND-80 Respect my contact preferences and quiet hours
LEND-81 Suppress all reminders for hardship-flagged accounts
LEND-82 Measure missed-payment rate per cohort
No reminder sent to any account with a hardship flag
Date moves re-amortise without extra fees
Opt-out honoured within 24 hours
Collections messaging
New credit assessments

actions.summary: Confirm no conflict with hardship and monitoring rules
actions.result: No conflicts; hardship flag must suppress reminders

actions.summary: Create a test-mode webhook for upcoming payments

scenario.outcome: Smart reminders are built in test mode and approved by compliance, with hardship customers excluded. Turning them on in production needs a release approval.

PROD-303 Fallback to keyword search on timeout
PROD-304 Per-stage analytics dashboard

actions.summary: Add the feature behind a flag

items: search/AiSearch.ts: query pipeline behind the ai-search flag
search/fallback.ts: keyword fallback on 2s timeout
flags.ts: register ai-search, default off
analytics: stage-tagged events
tests: 42 new cases, flag on and off
Unit and integration suites green
Load test at 2x peak with flag on
Accessibility pass on results view

actions.summary: Turn on AI search for 10% of users

sections.text: Setting the flag to 0% takes effect within 30 seconds; on-call has the runbook.

actions.summary: Compare search success and errors

scenario.name: Reduce discharge delays
scenario.why: Patients go home sooner, without touching clinical records.

trigger.msg: Discharges after 11am are blocking beds. What's going on?

steps.handoff: Pharmacy wait is the biggest delay

actions.summary: Analyse 90 days of de-identified discharge times
actions.result: 61% of discharges after 11am; pharmacy wait is the top delay

actions.summary: Map the discharge journey with ward staff

items: Medication charts finalised late morning
Transport booked on the day, not the day before
Families not told the discharge plan
Pharmacy queue peaks 10am–1pm
Paperwork waits for one consultant round
No visibility of bed demand downstream
Criteria-led discharge on 4 East pilot
Weekend discharge checklist

actions.summary: Add discharge plans to patients' records
Write the improvement options paper

fields.Reviewers: Director of Medical Services, NUM 4 West

sections.text: 61% of discharges happen after 11am. The longest wait is pharmacy: medications are requested on the morning of discharge.

items: Criteria-led discharge needs clear escalation rules
Lounge staffing on weekends
Pharmacy workload shifts to afternoons

sections.text: Pilot options 1 and 2 on one ward for 4 weeks, measured on before-11am discharge rate.

actions.summary: Draft the change and communication plan

scenario.outcome: The main delay is pharmacy, and three options are ready for clinical review with a one-ward pilot planned. No agent wrote to the EMR: clinical changes stay with clinicians.

scenario.name: Cut late deliveries
scenario.why: On-time delivery improves through better routing.

trigger.msg: On-time delivery fell to 87% in the north region. Fix it?

actions.summary: Analyse late deliveries by route and depot
actions.result: Late loads cluster on 3 routes leaving after 2pm

actions.summary: Check depot dwell times
Model the current and future dispatch process

artefact.title: Depot 4 dispatch: current and future process

fields.Evidence: 90 days of TMS and telematics data

items: Loads staged after 2pm compete for one dock crew
North cut-off at 3:30pm pushes departures into the peak
Average dwell at Depot 4: 48 minutes
3 routes carry 71% of the late deliveries
Pre-stage north loads by 1pm
Move the north cut-off to 12:30
Dock scheduling by route, published the day before
Second dock crew 12–3pm on Mon/Thu peaks

sections.text: Approve the 12:30 cut-off with the three affected customers before the TMS change is promoted.

actions.summary: Apply new cut-offs in the test environment

items: Cut-off for north routes: 15:30 → 12:30
Pre-stage flag required before tender
Dock windows assigned per route
Replayed the last 30 days in test: simulated on-time 94.6%
No orders orphaned by the earlier cut-off

actions.summary: Raise a change to promote the rules

scenario.outcome: Late loads were caused by afternoon departures from Depot 4. New cut-offs and pre-staging go live Monday, aiming to lift on-time delivery back above 95%.

scenario.name: Digital motor claims
scenario.why: Customers lodge motor claims online in minutes.

trigger.msg: Phone lodgement takes 25 minutes. Can we go digital for motor claims?

actions.summary: Analyse motor claim lodgement and cycle times
actions.result: 70% of motor claims are simple; lodgement averages 25 minutes

actions.summary: Prototype the online lodgement flow

items: Registration lookup confused 2 users: added a helper and example
Photo guidance cut retakes by half
Plain-language excess explainer improved trust
Progress indicator reduced abandonment in testing
Test the declined-cover path
Accessibility review with a screen-reader user

actions.summary: Create the digital lodgement epic

items: CLM-141 Lodge a motor claim online in under 10 minutes
CLM-142 Upload damage photos from a phone
CLM-143 See repairer options by postcode
CLM-144 Track claim status without calling
CLM-145 Fraud score runs before acceptance
CLM-146 Hand off complex claims to a consultant with context
Photo upload to 10MB, resumable
WCAG 2.2 AA
Fraud scoring under 500ms
Works on 3G connections

actions.summary: Lodge 50 test claims in non-production

scenario.outcome: Online motor claim lodgement is designed, specified and tested, cutting lodgement from 25 to about 6 minutes. Real claims are never paid or declined by an agent.

scenario.name: Month-end variance insight
scenario.why: Finance explains variances in hours, not days.

trigger.msg: Operating costs are 6% over forecast. I need the why by tomorrow.

actions.summary: Extract actuals by cost centre
Create a variance view in the sandbox

items: actual_amount − forecast_amount AS variance
variance / forecast_amount AS variance_pct
Joined on cost_centre and period
Excludes capitalised project codes
Row counts match GL control totals
No unmapped cost centres this month

actions.summary: Rank variance drivers
Check forecast assumptions
Draft the variance commentary

sections.text: October operating costs are $820k (6%) over forecast. Two drivers explain 80% of the gap; both are known and manageable.

items: Cloud spend +$410k: new analytics workloads, growth 14% vs 3% assumed
Contractors +$260k: delayed permanent hiring
Other +$150k: spread across 40 cost centres, no pattern

scenario.outcome: The 6% overspend is explained: cloud growth and delayed hiring account for 80%. Commentary and a reforecast recommendation are ready. No journals were touched.

scenario.name: Faster month-end close
scenario.why: Close the books in 4 days instead of 8.

trigger.msg: Month-end takes 8 days, mostly reconciliations. Help?

steps.handoff: Six suppliers cause most of the work

actions.summary: Analyse unreconciled bank lines
actions.result: 1,240 lines a month; 70% are 6 recurring suppliers

actions.summary: Create bank rules for the 6 recurring suppliers

fields.Created by: Business analysis agent, approved by you

items: Rules suggest matches; a person still reconciles
No rule touches payments or approvals
Audit trail records every auto-match

actions.summary: Confirm rules keep segregation of duties
actions.result: Controls intact: rules match only; approvals unchanged

actions.summary: Update the close checklist and train the team

items: Day 1: bank rules and auto-match, exceptions worked
Day 2: accruals, prepayments, intercompany
Day 3: review, adjustments, variance notes
Day 4: sign-off and reporting pack
Reconciliations: senior accountant
Journals over $50k: Financial Controller
Final pack: CFO

scenario.outcome: About 70% of reconciliations now match automatically, controls are intact, and the close drops from 8 days to a 4-day checklist. Nothing was approved, paid or lodged by an agent.

sections.text: Run the flexi pack as the lead offer, with monthly payments available at checkout.

actions.summary: Create the family renewal campaign as a draft

sections.text: Hi {first_name}, you were there for the big ones last season. This year, pick your 5: one family pass, any 5 home games, junior clinic included.

Day 3: SMS to non-openers
Day 10: call list of high-tenure members to the service team

actions.summary: Send the campaign to members

scenario.name: Early support for at-risk students
scenario.why: Students get help before they fail, not after.

trigger.msg: First-year attrition is 18%. Can we spot students who need help earlier?

steps.task: Agree what data can be used

actions.summary: Record the approved data use and privacy conditions

items: Use LMS activity and enrolment data only
Purpose: offering support, never penalties or progression decisions
Advisors see a flag and a reason, never raw activity logs
No individual-level data leaves the SIS or LMS
Students can opt out; opt-outs reviewed weekly

actions.summary: Analyse first 4 weeks of LMS activity
actions.result: No login in 10 days predicts 64% of withdrawals

actions.summary: Link to progression outcomes
Create advisor outreach tasks for this week's flagged students

items: Reason for flag, in plain words
Suggested opener: check in, don't check up
Links: study support, counselling, financial help
Outcome field feeds next week's review

actions.summary: Write the advisor playbook

scenario.outcome: A simple signal (no LMS login for 10 days) flags students early. Advisors have 212 outreach tasks and a playbook, under an approved, opt-out data agreement. No grades or enrolments were touched.

trigger.msg: Priority 1 response times are slipping on weekends. Why?

steps.handoff: The slippage is late weekend nights

actions.summary: Analyse the de-identified response-time extract
actions.result: Weekend P1 times +3.5 minutes, between 10pm and 2am

actions.summary: Compare unit availability by shift
actions.result: Unit availability drops 22% at shift changeover at 11pm

actions.summary: Model rostering options for the changeover

sections.text: Weekend P1 response times slip by 3.5 minutes between 10pm and 2am. Unit availability drops 22% during the 11pm shift changeover.

items: Workforce representatives on roster options
WHS review of extended shifts
4-week trial with weekly response-time review

actions.summary: Draft the trial plan and union consultation notes
